claims.text: Data preprocessing choices impact the reported accuracy measures of fairness-aware machine learning algorithms.
Data preprocessing choices impact the reported fairness measures of fairness-aware machine learning algorithms.
A large number of fairness measures tend to strongly correlate with one another.
Techniques optimizing for one fairness measure often perform well on different fairness measures.
Actual predictions made by different fairness-enhancing algorithms vary significantly from one another.
No single fairness-aware algorithm consistently dominates across both accuracy and fairness measures.
Fairness-preserving algorithms exhibit significant variability in fairness measures arising from variations in training-test splits.

Accuracy of SVM classifiers paired with Feldman et al.'s preprocessing is consistently higher when using numerical plus binary sensitive attribute representation compared to purely numerical representation.
There is an empirical trade-off between negative outcome group calibration (s-calibration-) and true positive rate (s-TPR) across fairness algorithms.

evidence.description: The authors find that input attribute encoding and transformation requirements impact accuracy measures reported in fairness literature.
Benchmark comparisons demonstrate sensitivity of fairness measures to differences in preprocessed data representations.
Stahel-Donoho correlation analysis across dataset-algorithm pairs shows high correlation among group-conditioned fairness measures and base-rate measures.
Empirical evaluation demonstrates that algorithms tuned for one measure routinely score high on closely correlated metrics.
Comparative results across five datasets show varied model predictions across different algorithm mechanisms.
Benchmark performance plots across all datasets show no algorithm achieving superior results in both accuracy and fairness simultaneously.
Evaluations over ten randomized train-test splits show large standard deviations in disparate impact (DI) and other fairness measures.
In all three SVM variants of Feldman et al.'s algorithm, accuracy is higher under numerical+binary representation across test splits.
Scatter plots of s-calibration- versus s-TPR on the Adult dataset reveal a clear trade-off line across evaluated algorithms.

methodologies.name: Open-source Modular Fairness Benchmark Pipeline
methodologies.description: A standardized benchmarking architecture that evaluates multiple fairness-aware algorithms under consistent data preprocessing, randomized train-test splits, and multiple fairness/accuracy measures.
conditions: Automated parameter grid searches for fairness-accuracy trade-offs

limitations.text: The study does not evaluate algorithms that seek to optimize individual fairness due to a lack of available implementations.
The scope of fairness interventions evaluated is limited to batch learning and excludes sequential or reinforcement learning paradigms.
Prior work lacks standardized data preprocessing pipelines and consistent testing methodologies across comparative evaluations.
Prior work often evaluates algorithms on a single dataset split and limited fairness measures, masking algorithmic instability.

future_work.text: Report algorithm performance metrics under multiple plausible preprocessing choices when evaluating fairness-aware models.
Report algorithm success and stability using a moderate number of randomized train-test splits to account for training instability.
Avoid introducing new fairness measures unless they behave fundamentally differently from existing metrics.
